column1: # Android is Kotlin and the backend is TypeScript, so the code is not shared.
# This file is. Both sides read THIS file and must produce the same numbers:
# A case added here is run by both automatically — neither side can quietly
# drift, and neither can pass by keeping its own private copy of the numbers.
# Format: tab-separated. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
#   field 1  label (what the case is about, in words)
#   field 2  input: a ledger written as ";"-separated tokens ("-" = no entries)
# Money is integer poisha (CLAUDE.md, D019): 1 BDT = 100 poisha, so 500 taka is 50000.
# Tokens. Each token is one thing that happened; the Nth token happened N
# minutes after the first, so the order in the line is the order in time.
# Positions are 0-based, and an undone entry is named by the position of the
#   credit:AMOUNT[@DUE]   addCredit            baki added by hand, optional due date yyyy-MM-dd
#   payment:AMOUNT        receivePayment       the customer paid this much back
#   sale:AMOUNT[@DUE]     completeCreditSale   one line, so the sale total and the baki are both AMOUNT
#   undo:N                reverseEntry         undo the credit/payment made by token N
#   unsale:N              reverseSale          undo the credit sale made by token N; its baki reversal is the entry
#   baki_balance   input -> the balance (calculateBalance), which may be negative
#   baki_overdue   "TODAY|tokens" -> the amount past its due date (overdueAmount)
#   baki_refused   tokens whose LAST token must be refused -> the word "refused"

column2: the Step 49 example: credit 500, payment 200, credit 100 -> balance 400
a customer with no entries owes nothing
a payment larger than what is owed is recorded and the balance goes negative
undoing a mistaken credit brings the balance back to zero
undoing a mistaken payment restores the debt
a credit sale adds what it totalled
undoing a credit sale clears exactly what it added
a sale, a payment and a hand-written credit add up
every kind of entry together
a credit with no due date is never overdue
unpaid and due yesterday is overdue
due today is not yet overdue
due tomorrow is not overdue
a part payment shrinks what is overdue
paying it all leaves nothing overdue
paying more than owed leaves nothing overdue
a payment settles the oldest debt first, and that one was overdue
oldest means earliest recorded, not earliest due: the overdue one is paid last
an undone credit is not owed, so it is not overdue
an undone credit sale is not owed, so it is not overdue
undoing a payment puts the overdue debt back
a credit sale past its due date is overdue
two overdue credits add up, one hand-written and one from a sale
a customer with no entries has nothing overdue
a credit sale entry cannot be undone alone; it goes with its sale and stock
an entry reversal cannot itself be reversed
the baki reversal a sale reversal writes cannot be reversed either
